artworks.title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
artworks.description: Ingres' Louvre masterpiece freezes the Theban roadside encounter: Oedipus stands naked before the winged Sphinx, answering the riddle of the creature that has been devouring travellers. Bones litter the rock while the hero's calm profile already carries the irony of a man who will solve every puzzle except his own birth. The canvas fixed the modern West's image of Oedipus as intellect facing monster.

artworks.title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
artworks.description: Moreau's Symbolist confrontation turns the riddle into erotic menace: the Sphinx clings to Oedipus' breast like a living puzzle, her feline body pressing against the hero who meets her gaze without flinching. Painted for the Salon of 1864 and now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, it made Oedipus a fin-de-siècle emblem of knowledge bought at a terrible price.

artworks.title: The Blind Oedipus Commending his Children to the Gods
artworks.description: Gagneraux's neoclassical canvas shows the aftermath of recognition: the blind king, eyes gouged, gathers Antigone and her siblings as he entrusts them to the gods before exile. The painting stages Sophocles' ruined Oedipus not as monster but as father — the curse made intimate. Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.

artworks.title: Oedipus at Colonus
artworks.description: Harriet paints the blind exile of Sophocles' last Theban play: Oedipus at Colonus, led by Antigone into the sacred grove where the gods will finally take him. The canvas turns the cursed king into a figure of tragic sanctity — the wanderer whose death will protect Athens. Oil on canvas, Cleveland Museum of Art.

films.title: Edipo re
films.description: Pasolini's desert Oedipus moves from mythic Thebes to modern Bologna — the king who solves the Sphinx and blinds himself, filmed as autobiography in sand and silence.

films.title: Oedipus the King
films.description: Saville's British adaptation casts Christopher Plummer as the king and Orson Welles as Tiresias — Sophocles in open-air ruins, the recognition played straight.

music.title: Oedipus Rex
music.description: Stravinsky's opera-oratorio in Latin, after Cocteau: the Theban king narrated like a ritual, the plague and the blindfold set to neo-classical steel.

popCulture.title: Oedipus Rex
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' Theban king who hunts a murderer and finds himself — the plague, the Sphinx's riddle, and the blindfold that still define Western tragedy.

popCulture.title: Oedipus at Colonus
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: The blind exile at Colonus, received by Theseus and taken by the gods — Sophocles' last Theban play, staged after his death, where the cursed king becomes a protector of Athens.

popCulture.title: Oedipus complex
popCulture.creator: Sigmund Freud
popCulture.description: Freud named a cornerstone of psychoanalysis after the Theban king — desire, rivalry and the family romance that made 'Oedipus' a word far beyond the theatre.
